newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island voters approve most local bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island voters approve most local bond issues.

text.p: Rhode Island's voters approved a number of local bond intitiatives, in addition to the approximately $230 million of issues that they gave the state the go ahead to issue, a state official said Wednesday.

Steve Klamkin, a spokesman for the state treasurer, provided the following list, based on reports from Providence Journal. The state official cautioned that not all the results have been counted, explaining some races still are close, as the following highlights make plain.
--Central Falls approved up to $12.5 million for pre-school expansion, and $3 million of sewer bonds.

--Chariho schools district, appears to have approved issuing $2.2 million of bonds for school computers and $2.3 million for improving school athletic facilities, although one of the three towns, Hopkinton, turned the bond measures down. Voters in Charleston and Richmond, however, approved them.

--Cranston, where a large number of mail ballots remain to be counted, appears to have approved $1.5 million each for the fire and police departments, $3 million for recreation bonds. Other bond issues, including $850,000 for Park Avenue bonds, $8.7 million for schools, and $600,000 each for public works infrastructure and equipment, seem less certain.
--Exeter, where mail ballots that have yet to be counted could prove deciding, voted on a $3.8 million school addition, and $1.5 million of highway bonds.
--North Kingston approved $2.2 million for new computers, and $2.3 million to expand and remodel school athletic facilities.
--Pawtucket approved $3.4 million for a range of projects from traffic signals to upgrading schools.
--Smithfield appears to have approved $425,000 of sewer extension bonds.
--South Kingston approved $1.7 million of recreation bonds and $300,000 for school facilities.
